holidays.name: National Cake Decorating Day
holidays.description: A sugary celebration for anyone who has ever wielded a piping bag with confidence, or at least with enthusiasm. Bakers and amateur frosting fans are encouraged to turn plain cakes into edible art with sprinkles, rosettes, fondant, and a questionable amount of buttercream.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that grew out of the baking community and cake-decorating enthusiasts, popularized through food calendars and social media. No single founder is widely credited.
holidays.funFact: Modern cake decorating took off in the 1800s after the invention of the pastry bag, which let bakers pipe intricate icing designs instead of just spreading frosting.

holidays.name: World Mental Health Day
holidays.description: An international day dedicated to raising awareness about mental health issues and encouraging open conversations, support, and resources. It is a reminder that checking in on your brain is just as important as checking in on your body.
holidays.origin: First observed in 1992 at the initiative of the World Federation for Mental Health, with support from the World Health Organization, which later helped make it a major global awareness day.
holidays.funFact: The first World Mental Health Day had no official theme, but since 1994 each year has featured a specific theme, such as workplace mental health or access to care.

holidays.name: World Porridge Day
holidays.description: A day to celebrate the humble bowl of porridge, from oatmeal and congee to grits and polenta. It combines cozy breakfast vibes with a serious mission to fight hunger around the world.
holidays.origin: Launched in 2009 by the charity Mary's Meals, which uses the day to raise funds to provide school meals to children in need. It started as a fun campaign tied to the idea of sharing a simple, warm meal.
holidays.funFact: The World Porridge Day campaign has included the Golden Spurtle, an annual World Porridge Making Championship in Scotland where cooks compete to make the best traditional porridge using only oats, water, and salt.

holidays.name: Double Tenth Day (Taiwan National Day)
holidays.description: A major celebration in Taiwan marked by parades, fireworks, flag-raising ceremonies, and festive public events. The name comes from the date: the tenth day of the tenth month, which makes the number 10 the star of the show.
holidays.origin: It commemorates the Wuchang Uprising, which began on October 10, 1911, and led to the fall of the Qing dynasty and the founding of the Republic of China in 1912.
holidays.funFact: The date is called Double Ten because of its repeated 10s, which makes it one of those rare holidays where the calendar itself practically wrote the nickname.

holidays.name: National Angel Food Cake Day
holidays.description: A fluffy, airy, cloud-like celebration of one of the lightest desserts ever to grace a dinner table. Fans enjoy it with strawberries, whipped cream, or just a fork and no shame.
holidays.origin: This is an unofficial food holiday that appears on national food day calendars, celebrating a dessert that became popular in the United States in the late 1800s.
holidays.funFact: Angel food cake gets its lift from whipped egg whites rather than baking powder or butter, and it is traditionally cooled upside down in the pan to keep it from collapsing.
